_comment: Expected results for fixtures/benchmark-artifact/v1 (issue #4), recorded independently of any pool implementation. Every value names the rule that derives it. Reviewed before implementation tests may cite this fixture as evidence. Derived hashes were computed with tools/build_fixture.py, a direct transcription of the pinned upstream convention (see README.md).

num_nonces.rule: num_nonces = num_bundles (2) x num_nonces_per_bundle (4, invented track t900; deliberately not a track from fixtures/tig/v1) per the sizing rule in fixtures/tig/v1/expected.json

tree_capacity.rule: next power of two >= num_nonces (schemas/member_protocol/v0.1.0/README.md, Validation beyond JSON Schema)

fee_paid.rule: base_fee 10000000000000000 + per_nonce_fee 1000000000000000 x 8 nonces (c001 fee config in fixtures/tig/v1/get-challenges.json; rule in fixtures/tig/v1/expected.json)

deadlines.rule: workflow_expiry_block = block_started + 120; package_due_before_block = workflow_expiry_block - proof_reserve_blocks (member_protocol.md §7 spike constants)

min_verification_quality.rule: Invented fixture threshold standing in for TIG's minimum verification quality (mining_system.md §8). Not a live protocol constant; see README open questions.

sampled_nonces.rule: Sample count 3 follows the c001 sample_counts convention in fixtures/tig/v1/expected.json; the specific nonces are a fixture choice standing in for TIG's published sample.

golden.description: Complete 8-nonce proof-material package. Passes JSON Schema validation, every mechanical check in member_protocol.md §10.2/§12, and sampled-proof verification.

manifest_bytes.rule: manifest.json is RFC 8785 canonical bytes with no BOM or trailing whitespace (member_protocol.md §10.2); this is the manifest SHA-256 declared at upload creation (member_protocol.md §11)

quality_vector.rule: qualities.i32le: exactly num_nonces signed 32-bit little-endian qualities in ascending nonce order (member_protocol.md §10.2); all >= fixture min_verification_quality 40

solution_signatures.rule: OutputData::calc_solution_signature = u64s_from_str(jsonify(solution))[0]: first 8 bytes, little-endian, of blake3(canonical JSON string of solution) (tig-structs/src/core.rs and tig-utils/src/hash.rs at pinned commit ad08d1ea001a73ff5aab3b556d7f59246fece14e)

leaf_hashes.rule: leaf = blake3(jsonify(OutputMetaData{fuel_consumed, nonce, runtime_signature, solution_signature} as bare JSON integers, keys sorted)) (tig-structs/src/core.rs From<OutputMetaData> for MerkleHash at pinned commit); leaf-hashes.bin is these 32-byte hashes concatenated in ascending nonce order (member_protocol.md §10.2)

merkle_root.rule: MerkleTree::calc_merkle_root: pairwise blake3(left32 || right32), unpaired node promoted unchanged, leaves not padded to capacity (tig-utils/src/merkle_tree.rs at pinned commit); must equal manifest merkle.root (member_protocol.md §10.2, §12)

proofs.rule: Branch entries are (depth, sibling-hash) pairs per MerkleTree::calc_merkle_branch; serialized form concatenates {depth:02x}{hash:064x}; MerkleBranch::calc_merkle_root(leaf_hash, nonce) must reproduce merkle_root (tig-utils/src/merkle_tree.rs at pinned commit). The complete ordered leaf-hash array is sufficient Merkle material for any sampled nonce (member_protocol.md §10.2).

expected_result.value: RECEIVED -> STRUCTURALLY_ACCEPTED -> DURABLY_ACCEPTED eligible; sampled-proof verification succeeds; TIG verification reproduces every record

bad-package-checksum.expected_check_result: finalize fails: whole-package SHA-256 of received bytes != declared package_sha256; package never reaches RECEIVED (member_protocol.md §11 finalize, §12 RECEIVED definition)

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15: 'A checksum mismatch in transit is retried and investigated; it is not a member penalty until the received bytes are stable and evidence establishes a member-originated bad package.' Member may retry or upload a corrected generation (§12). Escalates to MEMBER only with stable-bytes evidence; if origin cannot be established, UNRESOLVED (§15 table, last row).

truncated-upload.expected_check_result: committed_offset 24576 < declared 40960 at package_due_before_block 100191; finalize never valid; assignment cannot reach DURABLY_ACCEPTED before the deadline (member_protocol.md §7 deadline rule, §11 upload contract)

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table: 'misses the package block deadline while pool and TIG services were available' -> MEMBER; mining_system.md §8: missing the package-upload deadline before durable acceptance is member-attributable and chargeable once classified MEMBER
expected_classification.variant: if pool unavailability for the upload window is evidenced instead, attribution is POOL ('was unavailable for the upload window', member_protocol.md §15) and no member failure is recorded (mining_system.md §8)

missing-manifest-entries.delta_from_golden: manifest.json lacks files.leaf_hashes and merkle.root; member files are byte-identical to golden
missing-manifest-entries.expected_check_result: rejected before STRUCTURALLY_ACCEPTED: manifest does not conform to package-manifest.schema.json (member_protocol.md §10.2); missing required field is incompatible input, not a value to coerce (§14)

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table row 1: bytes match the declared checksum but structure is wrong -> MEMBER; mining_system.md §8: 'incomplete, malformed, or internally inconsistent even though the received bytes match the member's declared checksum'. Member may submit a corrected package generation before the deadline (§11, §12).

wrong-declared-size.delta_from_golden: manifest files.outputs.size_bytes declares 1038; actual outputs.ndjson is 1031 bytes (sha256 unchanged)
wrong-declared-size.expected_check_result: first failing check: declared file size does not match observed member bytes ('file lengths and hashes match', member_protocol.md §12 STRUCTURALLY_ACCEPTED; 'declared file sizes, SHA-256 values ... match', schemas README cross-field list; §10.3 declared-vs-observed enforcement)

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table row 1 (structure/consistency wrong with matching package checksum); mining_system.md §8 member-attributable list

missing-nonce.delta_from_golden: nonce 5 absent from all three member files; record_count 7 and file hashes/sizes are internally consistent, so JSON Schema passes and only the cross-field coverage checks fail
missing-nonce.expected_check_result: first failing checks: record_count 7 != num_nonces 8, quality bytes 28 != 4*num_nonces, leaf-hash bytes 224 != 32*num_nonces, output nonces not exactly 0..7 (schemas README cross-field list; member_protocol.md §10.2; §16 invariant 7: package covers exactly [0, num_nonces))

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table row 2: 'missing or duplicate nonce' -> MEMBER; mining_system.md §8: 'required nonce data is missing'

duplicate-nonce.delta_from_golden: output record 4 replaced by a copy of record 3 (nonce sequence 0,1,2,3,3,5,6,7); qualities, leaf hashes, and root recomputed so the package is internally consistent
duplicate-nonce.expected_check_result: first failing check: output nonces are not exactly 0..num_nonces-1 in ascending order (member_protocol.md §10.2; schemas README cross-field list; §16 invariant 7)

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table row 2: 'missing or duplicate nonce' -> MEMBER; mining_system.md §8: 'required nonce data is ... duplicated'

leaf-hash-mismatch.delta_from_golden: leaf hash for nonce 3 has its first byte XORed with 0x01 (a3 -> a2); merkle.root recomputed over the corrupted leaf array (64439b9d...) so leaf file and root agree with each other but leaf 3 does not reproduce from its output record
leaf-hash-mismatch.expected_check_result: first failing check: reproduced OutputData metadata hash for nonce 3 (a331b5d3...) != leaf-hashes.bin entry (a231b5d3...) ('every leaf hash reproduces', member_protocol.md §12; reproduction procedure in §10.2)

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table row 1: 'leaf hashes ... wrong' with matching package checksum -> MEMBER; mining_system.md §8 'internally inconsistent'

merkle-root-mismatch.delta_from_golden: all leaf hashes reproduce; manifest merkle.root last hex digit changed (…1c8f -> …1c80)
merkle-root-mismatch.expected_check_result: first failing check: calculated Merkle root d734f0c0…1c8f != declared d734f0c0…1c80 ('the calculated Merkle root matches', member_protocol.md §12; §10.2 root comparison)

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table row 1: 'Merkle root ... wrong' with matching package checksum -> MEMBER

identity-mismatch.delta_from_golden: manifest slot_generation 2 (assignment says 3), assignment_digest befce771d7742ea253242b6c6c2f821198d4f1364be6dc84e47bab433c93f1ca (digest of the slot_generation-2 mutation of assignment_identity, not the assignment's 1cd20851…), and versions.algorithm_binary_sha256 a54434b7… = SHA-256('fixture:algorithm-binary:WRONG') instead of the assignment's 4cce945d…
identity-mismatch.expected_check_result: first failing check: manifest does not bind to the confirmed assignment (assignment_digest, slot generation, algorithm binary digest all differ) — 'the manifest and assignment match', member_protocol.md §12; the manifest binds every identity, exact slot generation, and versions (§10.2); incompatibility fails closed (§14)

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table rows 1-2: identity wrong / 'wrong binary/runtime used' -> MEMBER
expected_classification.variant: if evidence shows the pool itself published an assignment inconsistent with confirmed TIG data, attribution is POOL (member_protocol.md §15 table: 'Pool issued an assignment inconsistent with confirmed TIG data')

solution-invalid.delta_from_golden: self-consistent package (own leaf hashes 4432c755… root) whose solutions are semantically worthless: quality vector [-1, 0, 3, -5, 2, 0, -2, 1], every value below fixture min_verification_quality 40
solution-invalid.expected_check_result: all mechanical checks pass -> STRUCTURALLY_ACCEPTED and DURABLY_ACCEPTED are reachable; mechanical checks 'do not decide whether a solution is semantically valid' (member_protocol.md §10.2). Screening/TIG outcome: zero bundles meet the minimum verification quality.

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table: 'Complete benchmark has zero bundles meeting TIG's minimum verification quality' -> no fraud attribution, chargeable tier failure unless a pool/TIG/compatibility incident applies; mining_system.md §8: such a benchmark 'counts as a chargeable failure for this tier policy even though it is not described as fraud'. Contrast: verified work that merely earns no qualifier is no failure at all (§15 table; mining_system.md §8).

method-non-reproducible.delta_from_golden: runtime_signature at nonces 2 and 5 is golden value + 1 (fabricated); leaf hashes and root (0301c853…) recomputed so the package is internally perfect. reproduction.json records the re-executed (golden) values; mismatch set {2, 5}.
method-non-reproducible.expected_check_result: every mechanical check passes; the package reaches DURABLY_ACCEPTED and the benchmark/proof are submitted. Later re-execution with the pinned binary, runtime, and assignment seed material does not reproduce nonces 2 and 5; TIG confirms the benchmark non-reproducible (terminal state FRAUDULENT).

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table row 2: 'TIG confirms non-reproducible/fraudulent member output' -> MEMBER; §15: 'a MEMBER method-verification outcome instead uses the separate method-loss rule' and does not increment f unless another chargeable failure also occurred; mining_system.md §8: 'Method-verification fraud remains separate: the pool ... charges the exact TIG loss under the method-penalty policy.'

scenarios_without_package_files._comment: Attribution contrast cases the Artifact Worker and fault attribution must also distinguish; they reuse the golden package bytes and differ only in pool/TIG-side events.

pool-lost-after-receipt.event: golden package DURABLY_ACCEPTED with receipt issued; pool later cannot read the artifact

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §12: 'If the pool loses an artifact after issuing the receipt, it is a pool failure and cannot be charged to the member'; §15 table: 'lost data after receipt' -> POOL; mining_system.md §8 not-member list; §8: after durable acceptance, member unavailability or deletion of local artifacts cannot be a member failure

pool-rejects-structurally-valid.event: pool rejects the golden package even though every §10.2/§12 check objectively passes

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table: 'Pool rejected a structurally valid package' -> POOL; mining_system.md §8: 'the pool incorrectly rejected a structurally usable package' is not member fraud

transient-network-retry.event: upload chunk fails with 5xx/timeout; heartbeats lost; member retries with backoff and completes before the deadline

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §13 retry rules; §15 table: 'lost heartbeat, or transient member network error by itself' -> no trust effect; §16 invariant 13: missing connectivity alone never becomes a trust penalty

unresolved-corruption-origin.event: received bytes unstable across retries; neither member-origin corruption nor pool/transit fault can be established

expected_classification.rule: member_protocol.md §15 table: 'Corruption origin ... cannot be established' -> UNRESOLVED; mining_system.md §8: record an unresolved operational outcome rather than automatically penalizing the member
